run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The hotel-reservation namespace holds a ResourceQuota memory-limit-quota (created 2026-11-24T02:00:04Z) whose memory constraint forces every admitted pod to declare a memory request. All 18 running pods and all deployment pod templates specify CPU only (requests.cpu=100m, limits.cpu=1) and no memory, so when the search pod was stopped at 02:00:04Z the Deployment search could not create a replacement: ReplicaSet search-567bb6c4b8 emitted 10 FailedCreate events with 'pods "..." is forbidden: failed quota: memory-limit-quota: must specify memory for: hotel-reserv-search'. Deployment search therefore has 1 desired replica, 0 ready/available, unavailableReplicas=1, and Service search has an empty endpoint set. Because frontend resolves backends through Consul and calls /search.Search/Nearby for the hotel list, every sampled HTTP GET /hotels returned 500 in 12/12 spans at 02:00:15Z, with the /search.Search/Nearby client span (12-37 us, error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR) as a child of the failing request and no search-side span present. Other paths are working in the same samples: HTTP GET /recommendations 200 (8/8), HTTP POST /reservation 200 (7/7) with reservation spans, HTTP POST /user 200 (9/9) with user spans, and profile/recommendation client spans carry no error, so the failure is isolated to the search-backed hotel list. Root cause is the namespace ResourceQuota; the search Deployment's missing memory request is the condition that makes it violate the quota, and the same latent condition exists in every other workload in the namespace.

claims.text: Deployment search in namespace hotel-reservation has spec.replicas=1 but no availableReplicas and no readyReplicas, with unavailableReplicas=1; its conditions are Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable, lastTransitionTime 2026-11-24T02:00:04Z) and ReplicaFailure=True with message 'pods "search-567bb6c4b8-gqz4h" is forbidden: failed quota: memory-limit-quota: must specify memory for: hotel-reserv-search' (02:00:05Z).

ReplicaSet search-567bb6c4b8 recorded 10 FailedCreate events between 2026-11-24T02:00:05Z and 02:00:06Z, each stating the pod is forbidden by 'failed quota: memory-limit-quota: must specify memory for: hotel-reserv-search', and a Killing event stopped container hotel-reserv-search in pod search-567bb6c4b8-zz5qf at 2026-11-24T02:00:04Z.

ResourceQuota memory-limit-quota exists in hotel-reservation with hard memory=1Gi, status.hard memory=1Gi and status.used memory=0; its creationTimestamp is 2026-11-24T02:00:04Z and its managedFieldsSummary shows manager OpenAPI-Generator performing an Update at 2026-11-24T02:00:04Z; no scopes or selector are specified in its spec.

All 18 running pods in hotel-reservation declare only requests.cpu=100m and limits.cpu=1 with no memory request or limit (for example consul-5c767d7459-bmjpn, frontend-68745cb99c-764hw, reservation-7d77c6cb59-27gmk), and no pod belonging to Deployment search exists in the namespace; the search Deployment's container hotel-reserv-search likewise declares only limits.cpu=1 and requests.cpu=100m.

Endpoints for Service search in hotel-reservation contain no addresses, while every other service in the namespace (frontend, profile, rate, recommendation, reservation, user, consul and the mongodb/memcached services) has one ready address.

In the frontend spans sampled between 2026-11-24T01:59:30Z and 02:00:16Z, 12 HTTP GET /hotels spans carry error=true, http.status_code=500 and otel.status_code=ERROR (durations 30-111 us), and 12 client spans '/search.Search/Nearby' on service frontend carry error=true and otel.status_code=ERROR with durations 12-37 us; the trace 3c8ad8fb0d779637 shows the failing '/search.Search/Nearby' span (1d19d976a38cd99c) as CHILD_OF the failing 'HTTP GET /hotels' span (3c8ad8fb0d779637) with no search-service span in the returned trace.

Other request paths in the same period are served successfully: 8/8 HTTP GET /recommendations spans have http.status_code=200 with child /profile.Profile/GetProfiles and /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations spans (frontend and profile/recommendation service) showing no error; 7/7 HTTP POST /reservation spans have http.status_code=200 with /user.User/CheckUser and /reservation.Reservation/MakeReservation spans on frontend, reservation and user services showing no error; 9/9 HTTP POST /user spans have http.status_code=200 with user-service /user.User/CheckUser spans showing no error.

The other 18 deployments in hotel-reservation (frontend, geo, profile, rate, recommendation, reservation, user, consul, jaeger, the memcached and mongodb workloads) each report 1 desired, 1 available and 1 ready replica, and all 18 pods are phase Running with every container ready=true and restartCount=0, so the outage is not namespace-wide runtime failure.

Consul service discovery being down was considered and rejected as the cause: the frontend logged 'grpc/lb/consul: error retrieving instances from Consul ... dial tcp 10.96.129.122:8500: connect: connection refused' only at 2026-11-24T01:59:49-01:59:50Z while the consul pod itself was starting (created 01:59:48Z), and at 02:00:15Z the same frontend successfully resolved and called profile and recommendation backends, which shows discovery was working when /hotels failed.

A crash, OOM or restart of the search application was considered and rejected: after 02:00:05Z no search pod object ever existed (no running pod, ReplicaSet reports replicas=0 and ReplicaFailure, all 10 events are admission denials 'FailedCreate ... must specify memory'), so the failure occurs at pod admission rather than in a search container, and no search container logs or last-termination reason exist to inspect.

The trigger condition for the admission denial is Deployment search's pod template omitting memory requests/limits while the namespace quota constrains memory; because every other workload in hotel-reservation also declares CPU only, any pod rescheduled during the quota's lifetime would be rejected the same way, so the search outage is the first visible instance of a namespace-wide admission constraint rather than a defect specific to the search image.

Add explicit memory requests (and limits) to the hotel-reserv-search container in Deployment search, and to the other workload containers in hotel-reservation, or relax/remove ResourceQuota memory-limit-quota, then let the Deployment recreate the pod and confirm Service search gains an endpoint and HTTP GET /hotels returns 200.

Check how ResourceQuota memory-limit-quota is delivered (its managedFields manager is OpenAPI-Generator rather than the kubectl-client-side-apply manager that last wrote the deployments at 2026-11-24T01:59:48Z) so an automated or manual apply does not re-create the admission block for every workload in the namespace.

gaps: No change_history integration is available in this Run, so who or what created ResourceQuota memory-limit-quota at 02:00:04Z, and whether the deployments previously declared memory requests, cannot be established; Kubernetes objects show only current state.

The exact mechanism that stopped pod search-567bb6c4b8-zz5qf at 02:00:04Z is not recorded: the events show a Killing of that pod, but ReplicaSet search-567bb6c4b8 carries creationTimestamp 02:00:05Z, so the ordering between the pod removal and the ReplicaSet creation remains unexplained.
No search container logs or previous-instance logs exist because no search pod was ever admitted after the quota appeared, so search-side application behaviour is unobserved.

Prometheus exposes no traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket or http_server_request_duration_seconds_count series for this target (get_metric_names returned nothing for those names) and the query for kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace="hotel-reservation"} returned no data, so error-rate and latency series for the failure are unavailable and impact is bounded by the trace samples at 2026-11-24T02:00:15Z.
Health of the rate service was not established: its log query for error patterns returned no lines but that view is not citable, and rate emits no traces in this Jaeger.

traces_search for the services reservation and user returned INVALID_PARAMS; their paths were instead assessed through frontend operation-filtered searches, so direct reservation/user service-level span groups were only partially seen.
next_steps: Add memory requests/limits to the hotel-reserv-search container (and review the same omission across the other hotel-reservation workloads), or correct/remove ResourceQuota memory-limit-quota, then confirm Deployment search reaches 1/1 ready, Service search gains an endpoint and HTTP GET /hotels returns 200.
Trace the origin of ResourceQuota memory-limit-quota (manager OpenAPI-Generator) in the deployment pipeline or fault-injection tooling to prevent the admission block from being re-applied.
Re-check whether other newly scheduled pods in hotel-reservation are being rejected by the same quota, since all workload containers currently declare CPU only.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
